## Session C: voting reasons without invented weather

Draft #4358 retires the zero-only weather reading from turnout. Six related tests passed. The drawn Homer year reached ten election results in 74.045 seconds; named and counted ballot records contain the remaining causes without a weather field.

## 2026-10-14 — Election day at the polls (`director/scenes-and-filters`)

- **On the eve of an election the player may vote in, the day stops at the polling place: the player stands there with the household members who may vote, and marks each race on the ballot (a candidate, or Leave blank), or leaves. The count that opens election day records what was marked.** Before, nothing let the player vote: every ballot was decided on the voter's own reasons. The visit reads the elections engine's contests and ballots and casts through the voting engine's `castBallot`. A player who takes "Election day" out of the scenes that stop their day votes or stays home on their own reasons, like everyone else. Measured in a played run on seed `4e24294a4208d1d8` (Koblerville, Northern Mariana Islands): the player lived day by day to the eve of November 3, 2026; Day stopped at the polls with five races and three household voters; after marking, the count recorded the player as voting, with each choice the one marked. The opening's marker and the first choices' glow now hold still under reduced motion. What failed: the first proof run stopped a day early, because the player clock's midnight is the start of the core's next day; fixed. No poll workers stand in the scene yet: the elections engine records no polling place for a precinct (stopgap `SG-PEOPLE-poll-workers`). Next: GOV's polling-place record, and mined lines for the scene (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-14 — The opening story (`director/opening-story`, #4157)

- **A new life opens with the President's address about the world the game made, full screen and cut by subject, then home that evening with the night's news to pick up and the first choices pointed out.** (Reworked the same day to the owner's direction: the shots-and-captions opening and its stopgap are gone.) While the world loads, the English engine composes the address from the macro engine's opening month against the year before ("Unemployment is at 4.1 percent. Jobs are up. Inflation is coming down."), the town's governor, and a place from the President's own campaign visits; the evening news carries the address and the town's area jobs figure. The opening shows the opening line and the remembered line over the existing rooms, the full text a tap away. The President now carries a home state, an office held before, the 2024 election and a visit to each state the real 2024 map shows as contested. Measured on three fresh seeds opening January 20, 2025 (Central, South Carolina; Hebron, Texas; Lindsay, Oklahoma): every address composed, with 11 sentences each, all from the mined bank with their record ids; build time on one seed went from 41.4 to 40.5 seconds (composition takes 8 to 21 ms). The played-world year (Sage, California, seed `33706e9a22452399`) passes with no new BROKEN verdict. What failed: no world said an ask of Congress, because the President's three issues rarely include one the President supports and the bill catalog names as an action; the bank has no crowd reaction, no "hard times" line and no inauguration sentence for the news, and the TV station has no named anchor. Next: an action phrase per policy question (OPUS-GOV), register cards for an address and a newscast (OPUS-PEOPLE), and mined lines for the address as a conversation subject (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-13 — MEMORY-FLAT, a town's memory (#4123)

- **"Generate a town" on the bench now builds the same two-level town as "New life"; a long game grows about a fifth more slowly; a town still costs about a gigabyte.** Measured on seed memflat-a (Washington, D.C.): heap after the opening went from 1,037 to 1,001 MB. Growth in years two and three went from 6.8 to 5.5 MB a month over 36 months. Measured in the played-world test on two seeds this session did not choose: Forest Lake, Minnesota held 463 MB after import and 1,167 MB after opening; Waipio Acres, Hawaii held 463 and 1,043 MB. The year took 12% longer in Forest Lake and 17% less in Waipio Acres, both within 20% of the base. Landed: retention for news, outcome-web landings and regional months; the two-level bench build; three memory ceilings in the guard, which the played-world test reports as known failures. In part: counted records no longer carry where each name was learned, rebuilt exactly at fill-in; the demo world builder left the core's imports. What failed: the 150, 250 and 5 MiB ceilings. The 463 MB after import is data tables for every place, owned by other engines. Counted people's past and traits (119 MB) can't be rebuilt from the seed one household at a time. Counted voting as groups would save only 4 MB, so it was not done. Next: a ruling on reading data tables from files on first use; OPUS-CORE's per-household generator and durable-log compaction.

## 2026-10-13 — PW-8, births and counts (`pw/births-and-counts`, #4095)

- **PW-8 (`pw/births-and-counts`): towns gain births, deaths and moves every month, and couples decide about a child from their lives.** On the first of each month each place's counted residents gain births at the state's NCHS 2024 rates by mother's age and arrivals at the ACS 2024 rate, and lose deaths by the SSA cohort life tables and departing households at the ACS 2024 departure rates. Which record changes follows its circumstances, never a roll, and one `counts` row per place per month records what moved. Measured in the played world on two fresh seeds. Candlewood Shores, Connecticut (`f5c4de6c3ad5f4c1`): counted people went from 41,103 to 41,605, with 438 counted births (53.0 per 1,000 women aged 15 to 44, against the state's 48.9 to 50.2). Ashaway, Rhode Island (`6370e560919024e3`): 39,364 to 40,084, with 343 counted births plus 3 full-person births (47.3 per 1,000, against 45.0 to 45.2). Every monthly row balances, and every dollar balances. The year takes 3 to 12% longer on the same seed; heap growth is unchanged. Full couples' plan-or-wait reasons now include income against the place's HUD median (no more −15.9 cliff at $0), work, room at HUD rents, health conditions, closeness, a smooth recovery pull after a birth, and an estimated start for undated partnerships. In the played-world test (`tests/golden-path/played-world.node-test.ts`) the counted population and births are real passes. What failed: a birth to a full couple happens in Rhode Island but not in Connecticut, where the only full couple was past childbearing age. Full-person births need young couples among the full people: BOARD item 4, OPUS-CORE. Early runs also showed a frozen carry row silently stopping later months' flows, copying 30,000-entry maps on every move, and couples planning again three months after a birth; all three were fixed before measuring. Next: OPUS-CORE's representative sample; newcomers into jobs and homes (`SG-PW8-counted-arrivals`).

## 2026-10-13 — PW-3, candidacy and votes (`pw/candidacy-and-votes`, #4097)

- **People decide to run, counted residents vote, ballots follow views.** About a year before a local seat's filing deadline every adult in town weighs running (named people through the chooser; counted residents from their counted records, filled in when drawn to run); races whose filing closed before the opening are weighed on the first day. Runners file when filing opens. Counted residents vote in local races from the incumbent's name, the party and how well known each candidate is, recorded by age group. Named ballots use the views engine's lean. Measured with the played-world test (#4091): Smyrna, Delaware (`10c6f008bceea9c5`) 13 named challengers in 22 races and counted votes in all 15 local races, all 16 checks pass, year 81 s on main and 96 s here; Vayas, Puerto Rico (`62e2547c4120986a`) 3 challengers in 45 races and counted votes in all 17 local races, year 79 s on main and 68 s here. Aua, American Samoa (`66597d61fb0276c7`) decided only its U.S. House seat in the year and nobody there chose to run, so "a named challenger runs" is now judged across towns, waiting on officials who are people (OPUS-OFFICIALS). What failed first: weighing only when filing opened left most towns with nothing to weigh; only named adults weighing left most seats without a challenger; counted runners piled onto one seat until a crowded-race reason was added; counted adults at their state's average engagement never reached the bar. Next: campaigns for resident candidates (`rivalCampaignDay` has no caller in play).

## 2026-10-14 — Election day at the polls (`director/scenes-and-filters`)

- **On the eve of an election the player may vote in, the day stops at the polling place: the player stands there with the household members who may vote, and marks each race on the ballot (a candidate, or Leave blank), or leaves. The count that opens election day records what was marked.** Before, nothing let the player vote: every ballot was decided on the voter's own reasons. The visit reads the elections engine's contests and ballots and casts through the voting engine's `castBallot`. A player who takes "Election day" out of the scenes that stop their day votes or stays home on their own reasons, like everyone else. Measured in a played run on seed `4e24294a4208d1d8` (Koblerville, Northern Mariana Islands): the player lived day by day to the eve of November 3, 2026; Day stopped at the polls with five races and three household voters; after marking, the count recorded the player as voting, with each choice the one marked. The opening's marker and the first choices' glow now hold still under reduced motion. What failed: the first proof run stopped a day early, because the player clock's midnight is the start of the core's next day; fixed. No poll workers stand in the scene yet: the elections engine records no polling place for a precinct (stopgap `SG-PEOPLE-poll-workers`). Next: GOV's polling-place record, and mined lines for the scene (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-14 — The opening story (`director/opening-story`, #4157)

- **A new life opens with the President's address about the world the game made, full screen and cut by subject, then home that evening with the night's news to pick up and the first choices pointed out.** (Reworked the same day to the owner's direction: the shots-and-captions opening and its stopgap are gone.) While the world loads, the English engine composes the address from the macro engine's opening month against the year before ("Unemployment is at 4.1 percent. Jobs are up. Inflation is coming down."), the town's governor, and a place from the President's own campaign visits; the evening news carries the address and the town's area jobs figure. The opening shows the opening line and the remembered line over the existing rooms, the full text a tap away. The President now carries a home state, an office held before, the 2024 election and a visit to each state the real 2024 map shows as contested. Measured on three fresh seeds opening January 20, 2025 (Central, South Carolina; Hebron, Texas; Lindsay, Oklahoma): every address composed, with 11 sentences each, all from the mined bank with their record ids; build time on one seed went from 41.4 to 40.5 seconds (composition takes 8 to 21 ms). The played-world year (Sage, California, seed `33706e9a22452399`) passes with no new BROKEN verdict. What failed: no world said an ask of Congress, because the President's three issues rarely include one the President supports and the bill catalog names as an action; the bank has no crowd reaction, no "hard times" line and no inauguration sentence for the news, and the TV station has no named anchor. Next: an action phrase per policy question (OPUS-GOV), register cards for an address and a newscast (OPUS-PEOPLE), and mined lines for the address as a conversation subject (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-13 — MEMORY-FLAT, a town's memory (#4123)

- **"Generate a town" on the bench now builds the same two-level town as "New life"; a long game grows about a fifth more slowly; a town still costs about a gigabyte.** Measured on seed memflat-a (Washington, D.C.): heap after the opening went from 1,037 to 1,001 MB. Growth in years two and three went from 6.8 to 5.5 MB a month over 36 months. Measured in the played-world test on two seeds this session did not choose: Forest Lake, Minnesota held 463 MB after import and 1,167 MB after opening; Waipio Acres, Hawaii held 463 and 1,043 MB. The year took 12% longer in Forest Lake and 17% less in Waipio Acres, both within 20% of the base. Landed: retention for news, outcome-web landings and regional months; the two-level bench build; three memory ceilings in the guard, which the played-world test reports as known failures. In part: counted records no longer carry where each name was learned, rebuilt exactly at fill-in; the demo world builder left the core's imports. What failed: the 150, 250 and 5 MiB ceilings. The 463 MB after import is data tables for every place, owned by other engines. Counted people's past and traits (119 MB) can't be rebuilt from the seed one household at a time. Counted voting as groups would save only 4 MB, so it was not done. Next: a ruling on reading data tables from files on first use; OPUS-CORE's per-household generator and durable-log compaction.

## 2026-10-13 — PW-8, births and counts (`pw/births-and-counts`, #4095)

- **PW-8 (`pw/births-and-counts`): towns gain births, deaths and moves every month, and couples decide about a child from their lives.** On the first of each month each place's counted residents gain births at the state's NCHS 2024 rates by mother's age and arrivals at the ACS 2024 rate, and lose deaths by the SSA cohort life tables and departing households at the ACS 2024 departure rates. Which record changes follows its circumstances, never a roll, and one `counts` row per place per month records what moved. Measured in the played world on two fresh seeds. Candlewood Shores, Connecticut (`f5c4de6c3ad5f4c1`): counted people went from 41,103 to 41,605, with 438 counted births (53.0 per 1,000 women aged 15 to 44, against the state's 48.9 to 50.2). Ashaway, Rhode Island (`6370e560919024e3`): 39,364 to 40,084, with 343 counted births plus 3 full-person births (47.3 per 1,000, against 45.0 to 45.2). Every monthly row balances, and every dollar balances. The year takes 3 to 12% longer on the same seed; heap growth is unchanged. Full couples' plan-or-wait reasons now include income against the place's HUD median (no more −15.9 cliff at $0), work, room at HUD rents, health conditions, closeness, a smooth recovery pull after a birth, and an estimated start for undated partnerships. In the played-world test (`tests/golden-path/played-world.node-test.ts`) the counted population and births are real passes. What failed: a birth to a full couple happens in Rhode Island but not in Connecticut, where the only full couple was past childbearing age. Full-person births need young couples among the full people: BOARD item 4, OPUS-CORE. Early runs also showed a frozen carry row silently stopping later months' flows, copying 30,000-entry maps on every move, and couples planning again three months after a birth; all three were fixed before measuring. Next: OPUS-CORE's representative sample; newcomers into jobs and homes (`SG-PW8-counted-arrivals`).

## 2026-10-13 — PW-3, candidacy and votes (`pw/candidacy-and-votes`, #4097)

- **People decide to run, counted residents vote, ballots follow views.** About a year before a local seat's filing deadline every adult in town weighs running (named people through the chooser; counted residents from their counted records, filled in when drawn to run); races whose filing closed before the opening are weighed on the first day. Runners file when filing opens. Counted residents vote in local races from the incumbent's name, the party and how well known each candidate is, recorded by age group. Named ballots use the views engine's lean. Measured with the played-world test (#4091): Smyrna, Delaware (`10c6f008bceea9c5`) 13 named challengers in 22 races and counted votes in all 15 local races, all 16 checks pass, year 81 s on main and 96 s here; Vayas, Puerto Rico (`62e2547c4120986a`) 3 challengers in 45 races and counted votes in all 17 local races, year 79 s on main and 68 s here. Aua, American Samoa (`66597d61fb0276c7`) decided only its U.S. House seat in the year and nobody there chose to run, so "a named challenger runs" is now judged across towns, waiting on officials who are people (OPUS-OFFICIALS). What failed first: weighing only when filing opened left most towns with nothing to weigh; only named adults weighing left most seats without a challenger; counted runners piled onto one seat until a crowded-race reason was added; counted adults at their state's average engagement never reached the bar. Next: campaigns for resident candidates (`rivalCampaignDay` has no caller in play).

## 2026-10-14 — Election day at the polls (`director/scenes-and-filters`)

- **On the eve of an election the player may vote in, the day stops at the polling place: the player stands there with the household members who may vote, and marks each race on the ballot (a candidate, or Leave blank), or leaves. The count that opens election day records what was marked.** Before, nothing let the player vote: every ballot was decided on the voter's own reasons. The visit reads the elections engine's contests and ballots and casts through the voting engine's `castBallot`. A player who takes "Election day" out of the scenes that stop their day votes or stays home on their own reasons, like everyone else. Measured in a played run on seed `4e24294a4208d1d8` (Koblerville, Northern Mariana Islands): the player lived day by day to the eve of November 3, 2026; Day stopped at the polls with five races and three household voters; after marking, the count recorded the player as voting, with each choice the one marked. The opening's marker and the first choices' glow now hold still under reduced motion. What failed: the first proof run stopped a day early, because the player clock's midnight is the start of the core's next day; fixed. No poll workers stand in the scene yet: the elections engine records no polling place for a precinct (stopgap `SG-PEOPLE-poll-workers`). Next: GOV's polling-place record, and mined lines for the scene (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-14 — The opening story (`director/opening-story`, #4157)

- **A new life opens with the President's address about the world the game made, full screen and cut by subject, then home that evening with the night's news to pick up and the first choices pointed out.** (Reworked the same day to the owner's direction: the shots-and-captions opening and its stopgap are gone.) While the world loads, the English engine composes the address from the macro engine's opening month against the year before ("Unemployment is at 4.1 percent. Jobs are up. Inflation is coming down."), the town's governor, and a place from the President's own campaign visits; the evening news carries the address and the town's area jobs figure. The opening shows the opening line and the remembered line over the existing rooms, the full text a tap away. The President now carries a home state, an office held before, the 2024 election and a visit to each state the real 2024 map shows as contested. Measured on three fresh seeds opening January 20, 2025 (Central, South Carolina; Hebron, Texas; Lindsay, Oklahoma): every address composed, with 11 sentences each, all from the mined bank with their record ids; build time on one seed went from 41.4 to 40.5 seconds (composition takes 8 to 21 ms). The played-world year (Sage, California, seed `33706e9a22452399`) passes with no new BROKEN verdict. What failed: no world said an ask of Congress, because the President's three issues rarely include one the President supports and the bill catalog names as an action; the bank has no crowd reaction, no "hard times" line and no inauguration sentence for the news, and the TV station has no named anchor. Next: an action phrase per policy question (OPUS-GOV), register cards for an address and a newscast (OPUS-PEOPLE), and mined lines for the address as a conversation subject (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-13 — MEMORY-FLAT, a town's memory (#4123)

- **"Generate a town" on the bench now builds the same two-level town as "New life"; a long game grows about a fifth more slowly; a town still costs about a gigabyte.** Measured on seed memflat-a (Washington, D.C.): heap after the opening went from 1,037 to 1,001 MB. Growth in years two and three went from 6.8 to 5.5 MB a month over 36 months. Measured in the played-world test on two seeds this session did not choose: Forest Lake, Minnesota held 463 MB after import and 1,167 MB after opening; Waipio Acres, Hawaii held 463 and 1,043 MB. The year took 12% longer in Forest Lake and 17% less in Waipio Acres, both within 20% of the base. Landed: retention for news, outcome-web landings and regional months; the two-level bench build; three memory ceilings in the guard, which the played-world test reports as known failures. In part: counted records no longer carry where each name was learned, rebuilt exactly at fill-in; the demo world builder left the core's imports. What failed: the 150, 250 and 5 MiB ceilings. The 463 MB after import is data tables for every place, owned by other engines. Counted people's past and traits (119 MB) can't be rebuilt from the seed one household at a time. Counted voting as groups would save only 4 MB, so it was not done. Next: a ruling on reading data tables from files on first use; OPUS-CORE's per-household generator and durable-log compaction.

## 2026-10-13 — PW-8, births and counts (`pw/births-and-counts`, #4095)

- **PW-8 (`pw/births-and-counts`): towns gain births, deaths and moves every month, and couples decide about a child from their lives.** On the first of each month each place's counted residents gain births at the state's NCHS 2024 rates by mother's age and arrivals at the ACS 2024 rate, and lose deaths by the SSA cohort life tables and departing households at the ACS 2024 departure rates. Which record changes follows its circumstances, never a roll, and one `counts` row per place per month records what moved. Measured in the played world on two fresh seeds. Candlewood Shores, Connecticut (`f5c4de6c3ad5f4c1`): counted people went from 41,103 to 41,605, with 438 counted births (53.0 per 1,000 women aged 15 to 44, against the state's 48.9 to 50.2). Ashaway, Rhode Island (`6370e560919024e3`): 39,364 to 40,084, with 343 counted births plus 3 full-person births (47.3 per 1,000, against 45.0 to 45.2). Every monthly row balances, and every dollar balances. The year takes 3 to 12% longer on the same seed; heap growth is unchanged. Full couples' plan-or-wait reasons now include income against the place's HUD median (no more −15.9 cliff at $0), work, room at HUD rents, health conditions, closeness, a smooth recovery pull after a birth, and an estimated start for undated partnerships. In the played-world test (`tests/golden-path/played-world.node-test.ts`) the counted population and births are real passes. What failed: a birth to a full couple happens in Rhode Island but not in Connecticut, where the only full couple was past childbearing age. Full-person births need young couples among the full people: BOARD item 4, OPUS-CORE. Early runs also showed a frozen carry row silently stopping later months' flows, copying 30,000-entry maps on every move, and couples planning again three months after a birth; all three were fixed before measuring. Next: OPUS-CORE's representative sample; newcomers into jobs and homes (`SG-PW8-counted-arrivals`).

## 2026-10-13 — PW-3, candidacy and votes (`pw/candidacy-and-votes`, #4097)

- **People decide to run, counted residents vote, ballots follow views.** About a year before a local seat's filing deadline every adult in town weighs running (named people through the chooser; counted residents from their counted records, filled in when drawn to run); races whose filing closed before the opening are weighed on the first day. Runners file when filing opens. Counted residents vote in local races from the incumbent's name, the party and how well known each candidate is, recorded by age group. Named ballots use the views engine's lean. Measured with the played-world test (#4091): Smyrna, Delaware (`10c6f008bceea9c5`) 13 named challengers in 22 races and counted votes in all 15 local races, all 16 checks pass, year 81 s on main and 96 s here; Vayas, Puerto Rico (`62e2547c4120986a`) 3 challengers in 45 races and counted votes in all 17 local races, year 79 s on main and 68 s here. Aua, American Samoa (`66597d61fb0276c7`) decided only its U.S. House seat in the year and nobody there chose to run, so "a named challenger runs" is now judged across towns, waiting on officials who are people (OPUS-OFFICIALS). What failed first: weighing only when filing opened left most towns with nothing to weigh; only named adults weighing left most seats without a challenger; counted runners piled onto one seat until a crowded-race reason was added; counted adults at their state's average engagement never reached the bar. Next: campaigns for resident candidates (`rivalCampaignDay` has no caller in play).

## 2026-10-14 — Election day at the polls (`director/scenes-and-filters`)

- **On the eve of an election the player may vote in, the day stops at the polling place: the player stands there with the household members who may vote, and marks each race on the ballot (a candidate, or Leave blank), or leaves. The count that opens election day records what was marked.** Before, nothing let the player vote: every ballot was decided on the voter's own reasons. The visit reads the elections engine's contests and ballots and casts through the voting engine's `castBallot`. A player who takes "Election day" out of the scenes that stop their day votes or stays home on their own reasons, like everyone else. Measured in a played run on seed `4e24294a4208d1d8` (Koblerville, Northern Mariana Islands): the player lived day by day to the eve of November 3, 2026; Day stopped at the polls with five races and three household voters; after marking, the count recorded the player as voting, with each choice the one marked. The opening's marker and the first choices' glow now hold still under reduced motion. What failed: the first proof run stopped a day early, because the player clock's midnight is the start of the core's next day; fixed. No poll workers stand in the scene yet: the elections engine records no polling place for a precinct (stopgap `SG-PEOPLE-poll-workers`). Next: GOV's polling-place record, and mined lines for the scene (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-14 — The opening story (`director/opening-story`, #4157)

- **A new life opens with the President's address about the world the game made, full screen and cut by subject, then home that evening with the night's news to pick up and the first choices pointed out.** (Reworked the same day to the owner's direction: the shots-and-captions opening and its stopgap are gone.) While the world loads, the English engine composes the address from the macro engine's opening month against the year before ("Unemployment is at 4.1 percent. Jobs are up. Inflation is coming down."), the town's governor, and a place from the President's own campaign visits; the evening news carries the address and the town's area jobs figure. The opening shows the opening line and the remembered line over the existing rooms, the full text a tap away. The President now carries a home state, an office held before, the 2024 election and a visit to each state the real 2024 map shows as contested. Measured on three fresh seeds opening January 20, 2025 (Central, South Carolina; Hebron, Texas; Lindsay, Oklahoma): every address composed, with 11 sentences each, all from the mined bank with their record ids; build time on one seed went from 41.4 to 40.5 seconds (composition takes 8 to 21 ms). The played-world year (Sage, California, seed `33706e9a22452399`) passes with no new BROKEN verdict. What failed: no world said an ask of Congress, because the President's three issues rarely include one the President supports and the bill catalog names as an action; the bank has no crowd reaction, no "hard times" line and no inauguration sentence for the news, and the TV station has no named anchor. Next: an action phrase per policy question (OPUS-GOV), register cards for an address and a newscast (OPUS-PEOPLE), and mined lines for the address as a conversation subject (OPUS-WORDS).

## 2026-10-13 — MEMORY-FLAT, a town's memory (#4123)

- **"Generate a town" on the bench now builds the same two-level town as "New life"; a long game grows about a fifth more slowly; a town still costs about a gigabyte.** Measured on seed memflat-a (Washington, D.C.): heap after the opening went from 1,037 to 1,001 MB. Growth in years two and three went from 6.8 to 5.5 MB a month over 36 months. Measured in the played-world test on two seeds this session did not choose: Forest Lake, Minnesota held 463 MB after import and 1,167 MB after opening; Waipio Acres, Hawaii held 463 and 1,043 MB. The year took 12% longer in Forest Lake and 17% less in Waipio Acres, both within 20% of the base. Landed: retention for news, outcome-web landings and regional months; the two-level bench build; three memory ceilings in the guard, which the played-world test reports as known failures. In part: counted records no longer carry where each name was learned, rebuilt exactly at fill-in; the demo world builder left the core's imports. What failed: the 150, 250 and 5 MiB ceilings. The 463 MB after import is data tables for every place, owned by other engines. Counted people's past and traits (119 MB) can't be rebuilt from the seed one household at a time. Counted voting as groups would save only 4 MB, so it was not done. Next: a ruling on reading data tables from files on first use; OPUS-CORE's per-household generator and durable-log compaction.

## 2026-10-13 — PW-8, births and counts (`pw/births-and-counts`, #4095)

- **PW-8 (`pw/births-and-counts`): towns gain births, deaths and moves every month, and couples decide about a child from their lives.** On the first of each month each place's counted residents gain births at the state's NCHS 2024 rates by mother's age and arrivals at the ACS 2024 rate, and lose deaths by the SSA cohort life tables and departing households at the ACS 2024 departure rates. Which record changes follows its circumstances, never a roll, and one `counts` row per place per month records what moved. Measured in the played world on two fresh seeds. Candlewood Shores, Connecticut (`f5c4de6c3ad5f4c1`): counted people went from 41,103 to 41,605, with 438 counted births (53.0 per 1,000 women aged 15 to 44, against the state's 48.9 to 50.2). Ashaway, Rhode Island (`6370e560919024e3`): 39,364 to 40,084, with 343 counted births plus 3 full-person births (47.3 per 1,000, against 45.0 to 45.2). Every monthly row balances, and every dollar balances. The year takes 3 to 12% longer on the same seed; heap growth is unchanged. Full couples' plan-or-wait reasons now include income against the place's HUD median (no more −15.9 cliff at $0), work, room at HUD rents, health conditions, closeness, a smooth recovery pull after a birth, and an estimated start for undated partnerships. In the played-world test (`tests/golden-path/played-world.node-test.ts`) the counted population and births are real passes. What failed: a birth to a full couple happens in Rhode Island but not in Connecticut, where the only full couple was past childbearing age. Full-person births need young couples among the full people: BOARD item 4, OPUS-CORE. Early runs also showed a frozen carry row silently stopping later months' flows, copying 30,000-entry maps on every move, and couples planning again three months after a birth; all three were fixed before measuring. Next: OPUS-CORE's representative sample; newcomers into jobs and homes (`SG-PW8-counted-arrivals`).

## 2026-10-13 — PW-3, candidacy and votes (`pw/candidacy-and-votes`, #4097)

- **People decide to run, counted residents vote, ballots follow views.** About a year before a local seat's filing deadline every adult in town weighs running (named people through the chooser; counted residents from their counted records, filled in when drawn to run); races whose filing closed before the opening are weighed on the first day. Runners file when filing opens. Counted residents vote in local races from the incumbent's name, the party and how well known each candidate is, recorded by age group. Named ballots use the views engine's lean. Measured with the played-world test (#4091): Smyrna, Delaware (`10c6f008bceea9c5`) 13 named challengers in 22 races and counted votes in all 15 local races, all 16 checks pass, year 81 s on main and 96 s here; Vayas, Puerto Rico (`62e2547c4120986a`) 3 challengers in 45 races and counted votes in all 17 local races, year 79 s on main and 68 s here. Aua, American Samoa (`66597d61fb0276c7`) decided only its U.S. House seat in the year and nobody there chose to run, so "a named challenger runs" is now judged across towns, waiting on officials who are people (OPUS-OFFICIALS). What failed first: weighing only when filing opened left most towns with nothing to weigh; only named adults weighing left most seats without a challenger; counted runners piled onto one seat until a crowded-race reason was added; counted adults at their state's average engagement never reached the bar. Next: campaigns for resident candidates (`rivalCampaignDay` has no caller in play).
